features.name: Title and its menu
features.what: The title row shows the focused conversation's title (or New Chat / Documentation) with a chevron menu to rename, archive or delete it.
entry_points: Click the title in the title row (chevron menu)

flows.name: See which conversation is in front
steps: Open a session from the sidebar
Start a new chat with Cmd-N
flows.expected: The title reads the session's title, then 'New Chat' for a plain chat ('New Conversation' in a folder), then 'Documentation'.
flows.why_hard: The title is drawn as a toolbar item and the window title is removed; reading it needs the window's toolbar or XCUITest.

flows.name: Rename the open conversation
flows.expected: The title row and the sidebar row show the new title; Rename is disabled for a conversation that has no session yet.
flows.why_hard: A SwiftUI .alert with a TextField (or a confirmationDialog) isn't reachable from an offscreen hosting view; needs XCUITest or a seam that sets the private @State.

flows.name: Archive the open conversation
flows.expected: The row moves to Archived and the pane forwards to a fresh session; the archived session's engine stops.

flows.name: Delete the open conversation
flows.expected: The session's log is in the Trash, its row leaves the sidebar, and the pane shows a fresh session.
flows.why_hard: A SwiftUI .alert with a TextField (or a confirmationDialog) isn't reachable from an offscreen hosting view; needs XCUITest or a seam that sets the private @State.

flows.name: Back out of deleting
flows.expected: Nothing changes: the session is still open and listed.
flows.why_hard: A SwiftUI .alert with a TextField (or a confirmationDialog) isn't reachable from an offscreen hosting view; needs XCUITest or a seam that sets the private @State.

features.name: New windows, tabs and folders
features.what: Opening another window, a tab, or a folder (from the File menu, Finder, the Dock or a second launch) gives it its own window and empty conversation.
entry_points: Drop a folder on the Dock icon / open it from Finder
Launch a second copy with a folder

flows.name: Open a project folder in a new window
steps: Pick a folder in the panel
flows.expected: A new window opens on that folder with an empty conversation and the where chip naming the folder; the folder joins Recents.
flows.why_hard: NSOpenPanel.runModal blocks and shows a system panel; needs XCUITest or an injectable panel.

flows.name: Open a second window
steps: Open Frog with one window on a conversation
flows.expected: A separate window opens on an empty plain chat; the first window is unchanged.
flows.why_hard: Key equivalents and menu-bar items only fire through NSApp's main menu; the offscreen test host never makes the window key, so the step needs XCUITest or calling the FrogWindow closure directly.

flows.name: Open a window as a tab
steps: Open Frog with one window on a conversation
flows.expected: The key window gains a tab with an empty chat (with no window open, a new window instead).
flows.why_hard: Key equivalents and menu-bar items only fire through NSApp's main menu; the offscreen test host never makes the window key, so the step needs XCUITest or calling the FrogWindow closure directly.

flows.name: Open a folder from Finder or the Dock
steps: Have Frog running with one window
Pick a project folder in Finder
With Frog running, drop a folder on the Dock icon (or open it with Frog)
flows.expected: The folder opens in a window of its own; the windows already open are untouched.
flows.why_hard: Goes through NSApplicationDelegate.application(_:open:) from Launch Services; needs a real app launch.

flows.name: Launch Frog again with a folder
steps: Have Frog running with one window
With Frog running, launch the same build with a folder argument
Check which copy is still running
flows.expected: The running Frog comes forward and opens the folder; the second copy quits. A different build (debug vs installed) runs alongside.
flows.why_hard: Needs two app processes and the lock file; the XCTest host deliberately skips the lock.

features.name: Quit guard and relaunch
features.what: Quitting while a conversation works asks whether to resume it next launch, and relaunching reopens windows and picks resumed turns back up.

flows.name: Quit mid-turn and pick it back up
steps: Send a message that takes a while
Choose Quit and Resume Running Sessions
flows.expected: The alert names how many conversations are working; after relaunch the turn continues where it stopped, before anything queued.
flows.why_hard: NSAlert.runModal from applicationShouldTerminate and a real relaunch; needs XCUITest or a process-level harness.

flows.name: Quit and stop working conversations
flows.expected: The turn is marked stopped by the user and does not resume.
flows.why_hard: NSAlert.runModal from applicationShouldTerminate and a real relaunch.

flows.name: Cancel quitting
flows.expected: Frog stays open and the turn keeps running.
flows.why_hard: NSAlert.runModal from applicationShouldTerminate.

flows.name: Relaunch to the same windows
steps: Open two windows on two folders
flows.expected: Both windows come back on their folders (the first pane's folder is the window's restored value).
flows.why_hard: Window restoration is disabled in the test host (restorationBehavior .disabled when testing).

features.name: Window drag and type-to-focus
features.what: The window drags from any empty space, and printable keys typed while nothing editable has focus land in the composer.

flows.name: Move the window by its background
steps: Open a window on a conversation
Press on empty canvas (not a control, grip or text)
flows.expected: The window moves; presses on the sidebar's or a pane's grip resize instead of moving it.
flows.why_hard: A real mouse drag (DragGesture or system drag and drop) can't be synthesized offscreen; only the post-drop state can be set directly.

flows.name: Start typing without clicking the composer
steps: Open a conversation with a few turns
Click a message in the transcript
flows.expected: The letters appear in the focused pane's composer; Cmd-shortcuts and arrow keys are not captured.

features.name: Phone and Handoff opens
features.what: A paired iPhone (or Handoff) can ask the Mac to show a conversation: it opens in the focused pane if that pane is a blank chat, else in a new pane beside it.

flows.name: Open a phone's conversation on the Mac
steps: From the paired iPhone, open a session on the Mac
flows.expected: The session opens in a new pane beside the focused one (or in place if the pane was a blank chat); nothing on screen is replaced. A test can post an OpenRequest notification in place of the phone; pairing is the settings agent's.

flows.name: Continue a conversation via Handoff
steps: Sign the Mac and iPhone into the same account
Read a conversation on the iPhone
Click the Handoff icon in the Dock
flows.expected: The same conversation opens in the focused pane.
flows.why_hard: NSUserActivity Handoff needs two signed-in devices.

features.name: Open a session from the list
features.what: Clicking a row shows that conversation in the focused pane, focusing it where it is already on screen.

flows.name: Open a past conversation
steps: Click a row in the sidebar
flows.expected: The pane cuts to that conversation's history, the row is selected, the title row shows its title.

flows.name: Click a row already on screen in a split
flows.expected: Pane 2 takes focus; A is not opened a second time. The row shows 'In pane 2'.

flows.name: Click a row open in another window
flows.expected: Window 1 comes forward with A; window 2 is unchanged.
flows.why_hard: Bringing another NSWindow forward isn't observable in a host whose windows are never ordered in.

flows.name: Open a Frog Cloud session from the list
steps: Create a Frog Cloud session from the web
flows.expected: The transcript streams from the gateway in the focused pane; the composer sends to the sandbox.
flows.why_hard: Needs a live gateway or a mock gateway wired into CloudSessions.

flows.name: Open a row beside the current one
steps: Find another row in the sidebar
Cmd-click a row (or right-click > Open in New Pane)
flows.expected: A new pane opens to the right with that session and takes focus.
flows.why_hard: The code reads NSEvent.modifierFlags / NSApp.currentEvent at click time; a test can't set those without posting real events.

features.name: Grouping, sorting and folds
features.what: The view options menu groups the list by Date (default), Project, Org (attention tree) or None, sorts it, makes it compact, and every group or parent can fold.
entry_points: Sidebar title row > filter (Group and sort conversations) menu

flows.name: See conversations by day
flows.expected: Top-level sessions sit under Today / Yesterday / earlier days with their started sessions beneath; the heading folds its day shut and open.

flows.name: See conversations by project
flows.expected: Pins as tiles, then one group per folder newest first, then chats; the chevron folds the group (remembered); Show more lists every row.

flows.name: See what needs me as a tree
steps: Have sessions that started other sessions
Switch the scope between Live, Today and All
flows.expected: Needs-you rows first (oldest first), then the started-by tree; Live folds settled work, Today adds what finished today, All shows everything.

flows.name: See one flat list
flows.expected: Pins as tiles, then every unpinned session in the chosen sort order.

flows.name: Change the sort order
steps: Have sessions with different names and ages
Sort By > Name (then Date Created, Last Activity)
flows.expected: Rows reorder; Cmd-1...9 follow the new order.

flows.name: Make the list compact
steps: View > Compact Sidebar (or Compact in the view options)
flows.expected: Rows drop to one line; the option is disabled while grouped by Org.

flows.name: Fold or show the sessions a session started
steps: Have a session that started two others
Click the caret on a parent row (or right-click > Collapse Started Sessions)
flows.expected: Children fold to counts ('4 running, 1 waiting'); clicking again shows them. The session on screen is never tucked away.

flows.name: Open the folded finished sessions
steps: Have a parent whose children all finished
flows.expected: The finished sessions list beneath; clicking again folds them.

flows.name: Reach older sessions on the same branch
steps: Run two sessions in the same worktree
Right-click a row with older sessions
Older on This Branch > pick one
flows.expected: That older session opens; the list keeps showing only the branch's newest.

features.name: Search the list
features.what: The Search row filters conversations in place, including the archive.

flows.name: Find a conversation by its words
flows.expected: Only matching rows show (by day; in Org their ancestors stay); clearing restores the list.

flows.name: Jump straight to the first match
flows.expected: The first match (or an archived one) opens and the field clears. In the other groupings Return does nothing.

flows.name: Find an archived conversation
steps: Have an archived session titled with a unique word
flows.expected: It appears in the results and opens on click.

features.name: Archive and unarchive
features.what: Rows archive from their menu, the archive is browsable from the footer, and quiet chats archive themselves.

flows.name: Archive a conversation from the list
steps: Right-click a row that isn't on screen
flows.expected: The row leaves the list and the footer counts it; what's on screen doesn't change. Archiving the row on screen forwards that pane to a fresh session.

flows.name: Look through archived conversations
flows.expected: The list switches to archived rows by day and back; the same switch is in the view options.

flows.name: Bring a conversation back
flows.expected: The row returns to the active list; the view doesn't navigate.

flows.name: Old plain chats archive themselves
steps: Leave a plain chat idle past the quiet window
Keep another quiet chat on screen
flows.expected: The off-screen quiet chat archives; the one on screen stays and the view never navigates.

features.name: Row menu: pin, rename, move and more
features.what: Each row's context menu pins, renames, re-parents, reveals, refreshes git, shows the session tree, and (behind the chief flag) makes a chief.

flows.name: Pin a conversation to the top
flows.expected: Pinned, it shows as a tile at the top (Project/Date/None) or with a pin glyph; unpinned, it returns to its group.

flows.name: Rename a conversation from the list
flows.expected: The row shows the new title (a closed session is renamed through `frog --rename`; a cloud one through the gateway after a short delay).
flows.why_hard: A SwiftUI .alert with a TextField (or a confirmationDialog) isn't reachable from an offscreen hosting view; needs XCUITest or a seam that sets the private @State.

flows.name: File a session under another
steps: Have a parent session with children and a loose session
Move to... > pick a parent (or Top Level)
flows.expected: The row nests under the chosen parent (or returns to the top level); a move that would nest it within itself is refused.

flows.name: Show a session's folder in Finder
flows.expected: Finder opens with the folder selected.
flows.why_hard: Opens Finder via NSWorkspace; needs a stubbed workspace to observe.

flows.name: Refresh a row's git state
steps: Open a project with a GitHub remote and a bound PR
Right-click a row with a git badge
flows.expected: The badge re-reads the branch and GitHub PR state.
flows.why_hard: Needs a real remote and gh, or a stubbed GitIndex.

flows.name: See the open session's fork tree
flows.expected: A popover draws forks off their source; clicking a node opens that session.
flows.why_hard: Popover from a private @State; needs XCUITest or a seam.

flows.name: Make a session the chief of staff (flag on)
steps: Turn the chief feature flag on
flows.expected: A wide chief tile shows first in every grouping; only one chief at a time; Remove Chief or archiving it resigns it.

features.name: Row state and hover badges
features.what: Rows show running, waiting, failed, finished-while-away and done, the pane number, bound PRs and a git badge whose hover card has the branch's state.
entry_points: Hover a row or its git badge

flows.name: Tell at a glance which sessions need me
steps: Start a turn in one session
Trigger a permission card in another
Let a third finish while another app is in front
flows.expected: Working spinner, amber waiting dot, red error dot, blue finished-while-away dot, then a green check that quiets once looked at.

flows.name: Hover a row to see its full badge
steps: Open a project session with commits ahead
Hover a row with a git badge
Rest on it past the expand delay
flows.expected: The badge expands in place inside the row and stays there while hovered.
flows.why_hard: Real pointer hover (onHover / onContinuousHover) can't be synthesized in an offscreen window that is never ordered in.

flows.name: Open a row's git card
steps: Rest the pointer on a row's git badge
Click it to pin the card
flows.expected: The card opens after a rest, a click pins it, Esc or a click closes it; scrolling the list closes it. Its git actions hand off to the inspector agent's Changes flows.
flows.why_hard: Real pointer hover (onHover / onContinuousHover) can't be synthesized in an offscreen window that is never ordered in.

flows.name: See a session's pull requests on its row
steps: Bind one or more PRs to a session
flows.expected: The row shows the PR count and worst state, matching the composer's status line.

flows.name: See which pane shows a row
steps: Open different sessions in each pane
flows.expected: Each open row shows 'In pane N'; Open in New Pane is hidden for rows already on screen.

features.name: Collapse, reopen and edge peek
features.what: The sidebar collapses to nothing, with a toggle (dot when something needs you) and New session beside the traffic lights, and peeks over the page from the window's left edge.
entry_points: Pointer at the window's left edge

flows.name: Hide the sidebar
steps: Open a window with the sidebar docked
Click the sidebar button in the title row (or Ctrl-Cmd-S)
flows.expected: The list is gone and the panes start at the window's edge; the toggle and a New session button wait beside the traffic lights.
flows.why_hard: WorkspaceView.toggleSessions is private and its button is a window toolbar item; a test can only build the view already collapsed (sessionsOpen:).

flows.name: Bring the sidebar back
steps: With it collapsed, click the toggle (or Ctrl-Cmd-S)
flows.expected: The list docks again at its last width.
flows.why_hard: WorkspaceView.toggleSessions is private and its button is a window toolbar item; a test can only build the view already open.

flows.name: See what's live with the sidebar hidden
steps: Let a conversation wait on you
Rest the pointer on the toggle
flows.expected: The toggle carries an amber dot; the hover list shows waiting, then running, then unread; clicking one opens it.
flows.why_hard: Real pointer hover (onHover / onContinuousHover) can't be synthesized in an offscreen window that is never ordered in.

flows.name: Peek the list from the left edge
steps: Move the pointer to the window's left edge
Move it back over the page
flows.expected: The list floats over the page with a shadow, then goes once the pointer leaves it; clicking its toggle while peeking keeps it open.
flows.why_hard: Real pointer hover (onHover / onContinuousHover) can't be synthesized in an offscreen window that is never ordered in.

flows.name: Toggle the sidebar in a narrow window
steps: Make the window too narrow for the sidebar and a column
flows.expected: In the narrow window the list floats over the page instead of docking; widening docks it.
flows.why_hard: Needs WorkspaceView's private toggleSessions after a resize; reachable only through the toolbar or the FrogWindow focused value.

flows.name: Dismiss a peek with Esc
steps: Peek the sidebar in a narrow window
flows.expected: The floating list (and any floating inspector) closes.
flows.why_hard: Needs a peek (private state) and onExitCommand, which only a key window delivers.

features.name: Resize the sidebar
features.what: The sidebar's hairline is a grip: drag between 220 and 400 points, double-click for the 250 default, remembered across launches.

flows.name: Make the sidebar wider or narrower
flows.expected: The column, its hairline and the panes follow the pointer within 220-400; the width is kept for the next window.
flows.why_hard: A real mouse drag (DragGesture or system drag and drop) can't be synthesized offscreen; only the post-drop state can be set directly.

flows.name: Put the sidebar back to its default width
flows.expected: The sidebar returns to 250 points.
flows.why_hard: Double-click on the grip needs real mouse events.

features.name: User footer
features.what: The bottom of the sidebar shows who is signed in to Frog Cloud with their credit (a click opens Settings > Billing), or offers sign-in with GitHub or Google.

flows.name: Open my account and billing
steps: Click the footer's name and credit line
Look at the window that opens
flows.expected: The Settings window opens on Billing (hand-off: the settings/account agent covers that window).
flows.why_hard: openSettings opens the separate Settings scene; not observable offscreen.

flows.name: Sign in to Frog Cloud
steps: Signed out, click 'Sign in to Frog Cloud'
flows.expected: The footer shows 'Signing in...', then your first name and 'Plan / $X credit'; cloud models and sessions appear. Hand-off to the account agent for the account itself.
flows.why_hard: Sign-in opens the system browser and waits on a callback; needs a stubbed CloudSignIn and a test account.

flows.name: Give up on a sign-in
flows.expected: Signing in stops without an error and the sign-in row returns.
flows.why_hard: Sign-in opens the system browser and waits on a callback; needs a stubbed CloudSignIn and a test account.

flows.name: Retry a failed sign-in
steps: Start signing in and let it fail
flows.expected: The footer says why in orange; Try Again reruns the same provider.
flows.why_hard: Sign-in opens the system browser and waits on a callback; needs a stubbed CloudSignIn and a test account.

flows.name: Notice I'm out of credit
steps: Sign in with an account at $0 and no plan
Look at the footer's credit line
Add a little credit on the web and look again
flows.expected: The credit line is orange; amounts under a cent read '<$0.01'.

features.name: New chat
features.what: Cmd-N, the sidebar's New session row or the collapsed title-row button start an empty plain chat in the focused pane with the composer focused.

flows.name: Start a fresh chat from the sidebar
steps: Open a project conversation with a turn running
Click 'New session' at the top of the sidebar
Look at the title row and the where chip
flows.expected: The focused pane shows an empty plain chat (title 'New Chat', where chip 'Just chat'); the previous conversation keeps running in the list.

flows.name: Start a fresh chat from the keyboard
flows.expected: An empty chat with the composer taking the keys; from Documentation it also returns to the threads.

flows.name: Start a chat with the sidebar hidden
steps: Click the pencil button beside the toggle
flows.expected: An empty chat in the focused pane.

flows.name: Cmd-N with every window closed
flows.expected: A new window opens on an empty chat.
flows.why_hard: Key equivalents and menu-bar items only fire through NSApp's main menu; the offscreen test host never makes the window key, so the step needs XCUITest or calling the FrogWindow closure directly.

features.name: New session in this folder
features.what: Shift-Cmd-N (or the palette's New Session) starts a fresh conversation in the focused pane's folder; a project header's + starts one in that project.
entry_points: Project header + / folder right-click > New Conversation Here

flows.name: Start over in the same project
steps: Send a message that takes a while
flows.expected: A fresh conversation in the same folder; the old one keeps its engine if it was mid-turn and finishes off screen.

flows.name: Start a conversation in a listed project
flows.expected: The focused pane switches to an empty conversation in that folder.

features.name: Empty conversation helpers
features.what: An empty conversation offers recent project chips, suggested first prompts for the folder and a setup line; model suggestions hand off to the models agent.

flows.name: Point an empty chat at a recent project
steps: Open a project once so it's in Recents
flows.expected: The pane switches to an empty conversation in that folder; the draft goes with it.

flows.name: Start from a suggested prompt
steps: Click one of the suggested starts
flows.expected: That prompt is sent as the first message.

flows.name: Act on or dismiss the setup line
steps: Open a project folder with skills or rules to add
Open an empty project conversation with something to add
flows.expected: The listed items are used, or the line goes and stays gone.

features.name: Type and send
features.what: The field takes text and sends on Return, with Shift/Option-Return for a new line, a round action button, and a draft kept per conversation.

flows.name: Send a message
flows.expected: The message appears as a turn, the field clears and returns to one line, the action button turns to stop.

flows.name: Send with the action button
flows.expected: Same as Return; with an empty field the button is dictate instead.

flows.name: Write several lines
flows.expected: The field grows a line (up to its cap, then scrolls) and nothing is sent.
flows.why_hard: The shift/option check reads NSApp.currentEvent at the moment AppKit asks the delegate; a test can't set it without posting a real key event.

flows.name: Press Return on an empty or blank field
flows.expected: Nothing is sent and nothing changes.

flows.name: Clear a long draft
flows.expected: The field returns to one line.

flows.name: Type quickly, or with an input method
steps: Type fast while the view re-renders
Compose a character with marked text (e.g. Japanese IME)
flows.expected: No characters are lost, the caret stays at the end, marked text isn't committed early.

flows.name: Leave a draft and come back
flows.expected: The draft, its attachments and the caret are back; each session keeps its own draft.

flows.name: Take Frog's suggested next message
steps: Finish a turn that offers a next step
See the ghost text in the empty field
flows.expected: The suggestion fills the field without sending; typing first hides it.

flows.name: Run a skill
flows.expected: A list of up to 8 skills shows above the field; the pick fills '/name ' ready to send.

features.name: Queue follow-ups and stop
features.what: While Frog works, Return queues follow-ups as chips above the field and the action button or Esc stops the turn.

flows.name: Add a follow-up while Frog works
flows.expected: A chip shows above the field; when the turn ends all queued messages go as one turn, in order.

flows.name: Take back a queued follow-up
steps: Send a message that takes a while
Click x on the first chip
flows.expected: That message returns to the field (kept with anything typed) and the other stays queued.

flows.name: Stop Frog mid-turn
steps: Click the stop button (or press Esc in the field)
flows.expected: The turn stops and the draft is kept.

flows.name: Interrupt from the menu
flows.expected: The turn stops; with a permission card up, Cmd-. is Deny instead and Interrupt is disabled.

features.name: Where it runs
features.what: Before the first message, one chip and menu choose a folder on this Mac, a Frog Cloud repo, or Just chat, with Branch and New worktree below.

flows.name: Run a new conversation in another project
steps: Open two projects once so both are in Recents
Start a new conversation and type a draft
Click a folder under This Mac
flows.expected: The pane moves to that folder; the draft, attachments and mode go along and the folder's remembered model and worktree switch apply.

flows.name: Filter the where menu or paste a repo URL
steps: Type part of a folder name
flows.expected: Only matching rows show; the pasted repo appears first under Frog Cloud.

flows.name: Use 'Choose a folder...'
flows.expected: At v0.7.0 this switches the pane to a plain chat (it calls switchFolder(nil)); no folder panel opens.

flows.name: Turn a project draft into a plain chat
flows.expected: The pane becomes a plain chat and the draft goes with it.

flows.name: Run a new conversation in Frog Cloud
flows.expected: The chip names the repo with a cloud icon; sending creates a sandbox session and opens it in the pane.
flows.why_hard: Needs a live or mock Frog Cloud gateway behind CloudSessions.

flows.name: Sign in from the where menu
steps: Signed out, open the where menu
Click 'Sign in to use Frog Cloud'
flows.expected: Browser sign-in, then the menu lists your repos (hand-off to the account agent).
flows.why_hard: Sign-in opens the system browser and waits on a callback; needs a stubbed CloudSignIn and a test account.

flows.name: Start from another branch
flows.expected: With New worktree on, the worktree is based on that branch; off, the checkout switches to it before sending (a dirty tree disables Branch).

flows.name: Send into a new worktree
flows.expected: A worktree is made, the pane moves into it and the draft sends from there; a worktree another engine holds is refused with its owner named.

flows.name: Send in the checkout itself
flows.expected: A notice says it works in the checkout; the message sends there.

flows.name: Recover when a worktree can't be made
steps: Open a git project whose worktree creation will fail
Send with New worktree on in a repo where it fails
Click 'Use checkout' in the status line
flows.expected: The error keeps the draft; Use checkout turns the worktree off and sends.

features.name: Permission mode
features.what: The mode chip sets when Frog asks (Ask, Accept edits, Auto, Yolo); Yolo asks once in the status line. The menu bar and palette set it directly.

flows.name: Change when Frog asks
flows.expected: The chip shows the mode and the next permission decision follows it, mid-turn too.

flows.name: Turn on Yolo
steps: Click 'Use Yolo' in the status line
flows.expected: The status line asks once ('Yolo runs every step without asking'); confirmed, the mode is Yolo and later picks don't ask again. Cancel keeps the old mode.

flows.name: Change mode from the menu bar
steps: Press Ctrl-Cmd-4 (Yolo) or pick under Model > Permissions
Look at the chip and the status line
flows.expected: The mode changes at once; this path does not show the Yolo confirmation.

features.name: Attachments and file drops
features.what: Images attach as chips above the field and other files become @ mentions, from the + menu, paste, or a drop anywhere on the conversation.

flows.name: Attach files with the + menu
steps: Pick an image and a source file
flows.expected: The image shows as a chip above the field; the source file is inserted as '@path' relative to the project.
flows.why_hard: NSOpenPanel.runModal blocks and shows a system panel; needs XCUITest or an injectable panel.

flows.name: Paste a screenshot
flows.expected: An image chip appears; text pastes as usual.
flows.why_hard: Paste reads NSPasteboard.general; a test would clobber the user's clipboard unless the pasteboard is injected.

flows.name: Drop files onto the conversation
steps: Drag images and files from Finder over the transcript
flows.expected: Images attach and other files become @ mentions; a screenshot thumbnail's file promise works too.
flows.why_hard: A real mouse drag (DragGesture or system drag and drop) can't be synthesized offscreen; only the post-drop state can be set directly.

flows.name: Remove an attached image
flows.expected: The chip goes; the text stays.

flows.name: Send just an image
steps: Attach an image with no text
flows.expected: The image goes as the message; a model that can't see images is named in the chip's help.

features.name: @ file mentions
features.what: Typing @ lists the project's files; arrows pick, Return or Tab inserts, Esc closes.

flows.name: Point Frog at a file
steps: Type '@' then part of a file name
flows.expected: A list of matching files shows above the field; the pick is inserted as '@path '.

flows.name: Start a mention from the + menu
flows.expected: An '@' is inserted at the caret and the file list opens.

flows.name: Close the file list
flows.expected: The list closes and the typed text stays.

features.name: !cmd shell commands
features.what: A message starting with ! runs that shell command in the conversation's folder instead of asking the model.

flows.name: Run a command without the model
flows.expected: A row runs the command and shows its output (rendering hands off to the transcript agent); no model turn is spent.

flows.name: Start a command from the + menu
flows.expected: A '!' is put first in the field, then the command runs as above.

flows.name: Queue a command while Frog works
steps: While it works send '!pwd' and another message
flows.expected: The command runs on its own, then the messages after it go together.

features.name: Dictation
features.what: The empty composer's action button (or Opt-Cmd-V) dictates into the field; a refused mic ends it with an error.
entry_points: Action button with an empty field

flows.name: Speak a message
flows.expected: The button shows listening; guesses are replaced as words settle; the text stays in the field with Send offered.
flows.why_hard: Needs a microphone, speech-recognition permission and real audio; SFSpeechRecognizer can't be driven in CI.

flows.name: Edit while dictating
steps: Type in the middle of the dictated text
flows.expected: Dictation keeps going after the edit without overwriting it.
flows.why_hard: Needs a microphone, speech-recognition permission and real audio; SFSpeechRecognizer can't be driven in CI.

flows.name: Dictate with the mic refused
steps: Click Open Settings in the status line
flows.expected: Dictation ends with 'Needs mic access to take dictation'; Open Settings opens System Settings > Privacy > Microphone.
flows.why_hard: The denied state comes from the system's permission prompt; needs a dictation seam to inject the refusal.

flows.name: Switch apps while dictating
steps: Switch to another app (or press Esc)
flows.expected: Dictation stops and the draft is saved.
flows.why_hard: Needs a microphone, speech-recognition permission and real audio; SFSpeechRecognizer can't be driven in CI.

features.name: Status line
features.what: One optional row at the top of the composer card shows the first of: an error with its fix, a question (Yolo, Merge, Archive), a notice, or the session's git state and next action.

flows.name: Fix what stopped a send
steps: Send while the engine is down (or signed out, or out of credit)
Click its button (Restart engine, Sign in, Add credit, Use local model, Retry)
flows.expected: The draft is kept; the button does what it says and clears the error (Add credit opens Settings > Billing, a hand-off).

flows.name: Dismiss an error
steps: Get an error in the status line
Click its x (or press Esc with nothing running)
flows.expected: The line falls back to git state or disappears.

flows.name: Jump to the changes
flows.expected: The pane's inspector opens on Changes (hand-off to the inspector agent).

flows.name: Commit from the composer
steps: Click Commit in the status line
flows.expected: Frog gets a turn asking it to review and commit; a hook failure keeps the message and offers Show output.

flows.name: Open a pull request
steps: Open a project with a GitHub remote and gh signed in
Click Open PR (urged when the work is done)
flows.expected: Frog gets a turn to push and run gh pr create; without gh auth the line offers Connect GitHub.
flows.why_hard: Needs a GitHub remote and gh auth, or stubbed GitActions.

flows.name: Push commits ahead of the PR
steps: If rejected, click Pull and retry
flows.expected: The branch is pushed; a rejection says the branch moved and Pull and retry never force-pushes.
flows.why_hard: Needs a real remote or a stubbed GitActions.

flows.name: Ask Frog to fix failing checks
steps: Open a session with a bound PR
Have a PR with failing checks
flows.expected: A turn 'Fix the failing checks on #N' is sent (queued if busy) and the draft is left alone.

flows.name: Merge an approved PR
flows.expected: The status line asks first; confirmed, gh merges that PR and the line moves to Archive.
flows.why_hard: Needs GitHub or a stubbed GitActions.merge.

flows.name: Archive a merged session
steps: Confirm if the worktree is dirty
flows.expected: The conversation archives and the pane forwards to a fresh session.

flows.name: Open or copy a PR link
steps: Open a session with a bound PR
flows.expected: The PR opens in the browser; Option-click copies its URL.
flows.why_hard: The code reads NSEvent.modifierFlags / NSApp.currentEvent at click time; a test can't set those without posting real events.

flows.name: See several PRs and bind another
steps: Type a PR URL or number in the field
flows.expected: The stack lists each PR with its state; the new one binds, or 'not found' shows inline.

flows.name: Check context and compact
steps: Open a conversation with a few turns
Click the context ring beside the mode chip
flows.expected: A popover shows tokens used of the window; Compact Now summarizes the conversation (hand-off to the transcript agent for the compaction banner).
flows.why_hard: Popover from a private @State; needs XCUITest or a seam.

features.name: Notices above the composer
features.what: Above the card the composer shows a cloud-unavailable notice, pending wake chips, a one-click next step, and a notice when another session swapped the machine's model.

flows.name: Dismiss 'Frog cloud is unavailable'
steps: Use a Frog Cloud model while the gateway is down
Read the orange notice above the composer
flows.expected: The notice goes; the reason text was selectable.

flows.name: See and drop pending wakes
steps: Start a background job or monitor in a session
See the chips above the composer
Click a chip to read its payload
flows.expected: Each pending wake shows as a chip; Dismiss all drops them and stops the pending timers and monitors in one action.

flows.name: Take the suggested next action
steps: Finish a turn whose next step is an action
See the button above the composer
flows.expected: The action is sent as your next message and the button goes.

flows.name: Dismiss 'another session swapped the model'
steps: Use a model on another machine
From another session, switch that machine to a different model
flows.expected: The notice explains the swap and goes on click.
flows.why_hard: Needs two sessions sharing a paired node, or a stubbed Devices.

features.name: Race attempts
features.what: Race sends the draft to several models at once from a popover; the race card itself is the transcript agent's.

flows.name: Race a prompt across models
steps: Type a prompt in a project
flows.expected: The field clears and a race starts in the transcript (hand-off). Race is offered only with words typed, not in a plain chat, not while busy.
flows.why_hard: Popover with a private @State, then several real model runs.

features.name: Model menu
features.what: The model chip opens a filterable menu: This Mac (Apple Intelligence, downloaded, one to get), Your machines, then Frog Cloud with prices; Manage... opens Settings > Models.

flows.name: Use a model on this Mac
steps: Click a ready model under This Mac
flows.expected: The chip shows the model and the conversation uses it; This Mac rows say '$0 a token' and their speed in tokens per second; Apple Intelligence is listed first.

flows.name: Download the model that suits this Mac
steps: Type and send while it downloads
flows.expected: The composer shows download progress and the action button shows loading; Return does nothing while it downloads (the draft stays in the field); when it's here the chat moves to the model and the draft can be sent.
flows.why_hard: A multi-GB download; needs a stubbed ModelDownloads.

flows.name: Stop or retry a model download
steps: Pick the 'Get' model in the model menu
While a model downloads, click stop in the composer notice
Click Resume (or Retry after a failure)
flows.expected: The download stops and the draft is kept; Resume or Retry continues it; a failure says why.
flows.why_hard: Needs a stubbed ModelDownloads.

flows.name: Use a model on another machine
steps: Click a model under Your machines
flows.expected: The chat uses it; a model not loaded is loaded there, after the machine's current turn if busy; problems show under the list.
flows.why_hard: Needs a paired node; MockNode exists in the tests and could stand in.

flows.name: Use a Frog Cloud model
steps: Click a model under Frog Cloud
flows.expected: The chat moves to it; rows show the price per million output tokens; small side-job helpers are left out.
flows.why_hard: Needs a signed-in Frog Cloud account or a stubbed model list.

flows.name: Pick a Frog Cloud model while signed out
steps: Signed out, click the model chip
Click a Frog Cloud row marked Sign in
Finish signing in in the browser
flows.expected: After sign-in the chat moves to that model and the draft is kept.
flows.why_hard: Sign-in opens the system browser and waits on a callback; needs a stubbed CloudSignIn and a test account.

flows.name: Allow cloud models for this project
steps: In a folder set to keep work on your devices, click a Frog Cloud model
Choose Just this conversation (or Always allow, or Keep it on your devices)
flows.expected: A sheet says where files and commands are sent; allowing picks the model, keeping declines.
flows.why_hard: A .sheet presented from the menu's private state.

flows.name: Pick a cloud model over the spending cap
flows.expected: The menu closes and Settings opens on Billing (hand-off to the settings agent).
flows.why_hard: openSettings opens the separate Settings scene.

flows.name: Find a model by name
flows.expected: Rows filter across all groups; Return picks the highlighted one.

flows.name: Manage models
flows.expected: Settings opens on Models (hand-off to the settings agent).
flows.why_hard: openSettings opens the separate Settings scene.

flows.name: Pick a model from the menu bar
steps: Open the Model menu with no conversation
flows.expected: The conversation switches; with no conversation the menu reads 'Open a folder to choose a model'.

features.name: Command palette
features.what: Cmd-K (or the toolbar's Commands button) opens a palette of actions, other sessions and documentation pages, filtered as you type.

flows.name: Open the palette
steps: Press Cmd-K (or click the Commands toolbar button)
flows.expected: A palette opens with the field focused and the first 12 commands listed.

flows.name: Run a command by typing
flows.expected: The list narrows by fuzzy match, the highlighted command runs and the palette closes.

flows.name: Close the palette
flows.expected: The palette closes and nothing runs.

flows.name: Jump to another session
flows.expected: That session opens in the focused pane.

flows.name: Change mode or model from the palette
flows.expected: The mode or model changes at once; the palette's Yolo skips the composer's confirmation.

flows.name: Compact, interrupt or fork from the palette
steps: Open a conversation with a finished turn
Open the palette in a conversation
Pick Compact Conversation (or Interrupt while busy, or Fork After Last Turn)
flows.expected: The action runs on the focused conversation (results hand off to the transcript agent).

flows.name: Show or hide Changes from the palette
flows.expected: The focused pane's inspector opens (hand-off to the inspector agent).

flows.name: Open a documentation page from the palette
flows.expected: Documentation mode opens on that page.

features.name: Quick switch shortcuts
features.what: Cmd-1...8 open the Nth top-level sidebar row, Cmd-9 the last, Shift-Cmd-] and Shift-Cmd-[ step through them with wrap.

flows.name: Jump to a row by number
steps: Have five top-level sessions in the sidebar
flows.expected: The third top-level row opens (children don't count); past the end the item is disabled; Cmd-9 opens the last.

flows.name: Step to the next or previous conversation
flows.expected: The next row opens, wrapping at the ends; from a session not in the list it starts at the top.

features.name: Session menu
features.what: The Session menu focuses the composer, dictates, interrupts, races, maps the project, compacts, sets detail, steps turns and forks.
entry_points: Session menu in the menu bar

flows.name: Get back to the composer
flows.expected: The focused pane's composer takes the keyboard; from Documentation it also returns to the threads.

flows.name: Map the project's structure
steps: Open a project with source files
Look at the new window (or the composer's notice)
flows.expected: A Diagram window opens with the code map; a folder without dependent files flashes 'Couldn't map this folder' in the composer.
flows.why_hard: The code map opens in a separate Diagram window through openWindow, which an offscreen host can't observe; the failure notice path is reachable.

flows.name: Compact the conversation
steps: After a few turns, press Shift-Cmd-K
flows.expected: Frog summarizes to free context (hand-off to the transcript agent); disabled while busy or empty.

flows.name: Change how much detail the transcript shows
steps: Open a conversation with tool calls
flows.expected: This conversation's detail changes (hand-off to the transcript agent); Default follows the app setting.

flows.name: Step through turns
steps: Open a conversation with several turns
flows.expected: The transcript scrolls to the previous or next turn (hand-off to the transcript agent).

flows.name: Fork after the last turn
flows.expected: A new session forked after that turn opens (hand-off to the transcript agent for its rows).

features.name: Edit menu: undo turn and find
features.what: Edit gains Undo Last Turn (with a confirmation) and Find in Conversation with Find Next and Previous.

flows.name: Undo the last turn's file changes
steps: After a turn that edited files, press Opt-Cmd-Z
flows.expected: A dialog names the turn; confirmed, its edits revert and the conversation continues from before it (hand-off to the transcript agent).
flows.why_hard: A SwiftUI .alert with a TextField (or a confirmationDialog) isn't reachable from an offscreen hosting view; needs XCUITest or a seam that sets the private @State.

flows.name: Find text in the conversation
steps: Press Return or Cmd-G, then Shift-Cmd-G
flows.expected: A find bar shows 'N of M', steps through matching turns (marked on the timeline rail) and closes.

features.name: View menu: panels
features.what: View toggles the sidebar and the focused pane's inspector and opens Terminal, Preview and Inspect Element; the toolbar has the same Inspector button.

flows.name: Toggle the sidebar from the keyboard
steps: Open a window with the sidebar docked
Look at the View menu's item title
flows.expected: The sidebar hides then shows; the menu item's title follows (Hide/Show Sessions).
flows.why_hard: WorkspaceView.toggleSessions is private; only reachable through the FrogWindow focused value or XCUITest.

flows.name: Open Changes, Terminal or Preview
flows.expected: The focused pane's inspector opens on that tab, floating when the window is too narrow (the panels are the inspector agent's).

features.name: Escape
features.what: Esc backs out of the innermost thing: Documentation, then a maximized pane, then the find bar, then any peek.

flows.name: Back out with Esc
steps: Maximize a pane and open Find
flows.expected: The first Esc restores the panes, the next closes the find bar; in Documentation Esc goes back to the app first.
flows.why_hard: onExitCommand needs a key window and a real cancelOperation; reachable only through XCUITest.

features.name: App menu hand-offs
features.what: Frog > Settings (Cmd-,) and Check for Updates live in the app menu and belong to the settings and updates agent.

flows.name: Open Settings
steps: Look at which tab it opens on
flows.expected: The separate Settings window opens on the last tab (hand-off to the settings agent; there is no Settings row in the Mac sidebar at v0.7.0).
flows.why_hard: Settings is its own scene; needs XCUITest.

features.name: Split panes
features.what: A window holds up to four conversations side by side or stacked; the focused pane is the one menus act on, each has its own composer and inspector.
entry_points: Row menu > Open in New Pane
Drag a row onto a pane

flows.name: Work on two things side by side
steps: Click the Split toolbar button (or Cmd-\)
Look at which composer is at full strength
flows.expected: A new pane opens to the right on a fresh conversation in the same folder and takes focus; no pane has a header.

flows.name: Stack two conversations
steps: Press Shift-Cmd-\ (or right-click Split > Split Down)
flows.expected: A new pane opens below the focused one.

flows.name: Split further
flows.expected: Panes share the width evenly; at four panes Split is disabled.

flows.name: Open a sidebar row beside the current one
flows.expected: The session opens in a new pane to the right; if it's already on screen that pane is focused instead.

flows.name: Drag a conversation into place
steps: Drag a sidebar row over a pane's right edge
Drop on 'Split right' (or the middle for 'Open here')
flows.expected: The drop zone and a title capsule follow the pointer; the session opens in a new pane there or replaces that pane's; one already on screen moves instead.
flows.why_hard: A real mouse drag (DragGesture or system drag and drop) can't be synthesized offscreen; only the post-drop state can be set directly.

flows.name: Choose which pane I'm working in
steps: Click anywhere in the other pane
flows.expected: That pane's composer comes to full strength and the other steps back; the title row, menus and palette act on it.

flows.name: Move focus between panes
steps: Split the window into three panes
flows.expected: Focus moves to the next or previous pane (wrapping) and its composer takes the keyboard.

flows.name: Close a pane
steps: Split the window into two panes
Focus a pane in a split
flows.expected: The pane goes, its engine stops, the rest fill the space and focus moves; the item is disabled when unsplit.

flows.name: Give one pane the whole window
flows.expected: The pane fills the canvas with no dividers; restoring brings back the exact layout.

flows.name: Resize panes
steps: Hover the line between two panes
flows.expected: The panes follow the pointer down to their floors (360, or 260 beside a terminal or preview); double-click evens them out.
flows.why_hard: A real mouse drag (DragGesture or system drag and drop) can't be synthesized offscreen; only the post-drop state can be set directly.

flows.name: Use an inspector per pane
steps: Split with a conversation that has changes in each pane
flows.expected: Each pane docks its own inspector; the top-right one's tabs sit in the title row, the other's on the sidebar's first row (inspector contents are the inspector agent's).

features.name: Documentation mode
features.what: The shell swaps the thread list for the docs' page list and the main area for one page; Back to app returns to exactly where you were.

flows.name: Open the documentation
steps: Click Documentation at the bottom of the sidebar
Look at the sidebar, title and toolbar
flows.expected: The sidebar shows Back to app, Search docs and pages by section with the build's version; the page shows; the title reads Documentation; split and inspector are disabled.

flows.name: Open documentation from Help
steps: Look at the sidebar and title
flows.expected: Same as the sidebar row, on the page last shown.

flows.name: Read another page
steps: Click a page in the docs sidebar
flows.expected: The page shows from the top with the selected row style; Previous/Next cross sections.

flows.name: Search the documentation
flows.expected: Pages filter by title and heading ('No pages match' when none); Return opens the first; Esc clears, then leaves docs.

flows.name: Go back to my conversation
steps: Type a draft and open an inspector tab
Click Back to app (or Esc, Cmd-L, Cmd-N)
flows.expected: The same thread, scroll position, draft and inspector tab are back, and a running turn never stopped; the composer takes the keyboard.

flows.name: Come back to the page I was reading
flows.expected: It opens on the page last shown, for the life of the window.

flows.name: Share a docs page
steps: On a page, click Open on the web
flows.expected: The browser opens frog.toys/docs/<slug>.

flows.name: Read the Mac's version of a page
steps: Open a page with platform blocks
flows.expected: Mac-only blocks show, web- and terminal-only ones don't.

flows.name: Type while reading docs
steps: Open a conversation with an empty composer
flows.expected: Nothing lands in the hidden composer's draft.

flows.name: Hide the page list
steps: In Documentation, click the sidebar button (or Ctrl-Cmd-S)
flows.expected: The page list collapses like the thread list and comes back the same way.
